electrolysis-plating.alt: A beaker of copper(II) sulfate with a copper anode and a key as the cathode, joined to a power supply that moves electrons from the anode to the key. Copper dissolves at the anode and plates onto the key. Below, a chain: current times time gives charge; divide by F for moles of electrons; divide by 2 for moles of copper; multiply by 63.55 for grams of copper.
